BiblicalUsage: The word means to complain, to murmur against what God has done: when the people complained, it displeased the LORD, and the fire of the LORD burnt among them. Jeremiah asks why a living man should complain at all, a man punished for his sins. The same word is the crowd grumbling in the wilderness and the prophet's question.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for complaining carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Jeremiah's question — a living man, punished for his sins, has nothing to complain about.
